country: South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Kenya, Ghana

links.outcome: Model performance in own site versus other, unseen sites for active convulsive epilepsy
links.effect: Single-site models performed well within their own regions but worse on other regions (p<0.05); model weights and optimal thresholds varied markedly across sites.
links.quote: Single-site clinical models performed well within their own regions, but worse in general when evaluated on other regions (p<0.05).

links.outcome: Variation in model performance and parameters across sites
links.effect: Performance dropped when models were applied to other sites; thresholds and weights varied across sites. Multi-site training lowered mean internal performance while external performance improved.
links.quote: Model weights and optimal thresholds varied markedly across sites.

unlisted_practices: Multi-site training to improve external generalisability, with a trade-off against internal performance
Leave-one-site-out cross-validation to assess each site's contribution

screen.reason: The study directly investigates cross-site generalizability and evaluates practices for model deployment across diverse low-resource settings, specifically measuring the impact of pooling multi-site training data and assessing site-specific optimal threshold variation.

primary.practice: multi-site training and local threshold calibration
